'''Stanford Solomon Penner''' (5 July 1921 – 15 July 2016) also known as '''Sol Penner''', was a German-American scientist and engineer, a major figure in combustion physics, especially in rocket engines, and a founder of the Engineering program at [[University of California, San Diego]]. He obtained his PhD in 1946 from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] under [[Farrington Daniels]] and [[Theodore von Kármán]].

== Biography ==
Stanford S. Penner was born on July 5, 1921, in [[Unna]], Germany, a small town in the [[North Rhine-Westphalia]] region of Germany. He moved to the U.S. when he was 15 and he earned his bachelor's degree in chemistry at [[Union College]] in New York in 1942. He obtained his PhD from the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] under the supervision of [[Farrington Daniels]] and [[Theodore von Kármán]], specializing in the development of rocket engines, and became a researcher at [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] after finishing his doctorate.

After working as a research engineer at [[Jet Propulsion Laboratory]] from 1946 to 1950, he became the Professor of Jet Propulsion at [[Caltech]] from 1950 to 1964. At 1964, he came to [[UCSD]] as a founding chair of the [[UCSD]]'s first engineering department. In 1972, he created the [[Center for Energy Research]] at [[UCSD]] as a place for researchers from across campus and around the world to come together to pursue critical, interdisciplinary energy research.

Penner died at his home in [[La Jolla]] on July 15, 2016, at the age of 95.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ucsdnews.ucsd.edu/pressrelease/remembering_stanford_sol_penner_a_founding_engineering_professor_at_uc_san |title=Remembering Stanford 'Sol' Penner, a Founding Engineering Professor at UC San Diego |publisher=Ucsdnews.ucsd.edu |date=2016-07-20 |access-date=2017-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mae.ucsd.edu/node/92 |title=The Stanford S. and Beverly P. Penner Distinguished Lectures in the Mechanical & Aerospace Engineering {{pipe}} Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering |publisher=Mae.ucsd.edu |access-date=2017-05-08|url-status=usurped}}</ref>

==Research==

Penner<ref>{{cite journal |doi=10.1146/annurev.fluid.010908.165156 |title=Von Kármán's Work: The Later Years (1952 to 1963) and Legacy |journal=Annual Review of Fluid Mechanics |volume=41 |pages=1–15 |year=2009 |last1=Penner |first1=S.S |last2=Williams |first2=F.A |last3=Libby |first3=P.A |last4=Nemat-Nasser |first4=S }}</ref> collaborated with [[Theodore von Kármán]] in the later years of [[Theodore von Kármán|von Kármán]] life for 15 years. The Kármán–Penner flux fraction, first introduced by Von Kármán and Penner in 1954, is the fraction of mass flux of a particular chemical species (it is used sometimes in place of species mass fraction).<ref>Von Karman, T., & Penner, S. S. (1954). Selected combustion problems. II, AGARD, 167.</ref><ref>von Karman, T., & Penner, S. S. (1954). Fundamental approach to laminar flame propagation.</ref><ref>von Karman, T., & Penner, S. S. (1954). The thermal theory of constant-pressure deflagration for first-order global reactions.</ref> He has received numerous professional honors, including election to the National Academy of Engineering, the American Academy of Arts and Sciences, the International Academy of Astronautics; he has also been awarded the Distinguished Associate Award from the US Department of Energy and the Founders Award from the National Academy of Engineering.<ref>Williams, Forman Arthur, et al., eds. Modern Developments in Energy, Combustion and Spectroscopy: In Honor of SS Penner. Elsevier, 2013.</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://mae.princeton.edu/about-mae/news/howard-stone-gave-stanford-s-and-beverley-p-penner-distinguished-lecture |title=Howard Stone gave the Stanford S. and Beverley P. Penner Distinguished Lecture {{pipe}} Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering |publisher=Mae.princeton.edu |access-date=2017-05-08}}</ref>

Penner also founded two scientific journals: the ''[[Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer]]'' in 1961, serving as chief editor for over 30 years and in 1975 he founded ''Energy, An International Journal'' and of the (classified) Journal of Defense Research.

==Publications==
Penner<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nae.edu/55565.aspx |title=NAE Website – Dr. Stanford "Sol" Penner |publisher=Nae.edu |access-date=2017-05-08}}</ref> has published around 320 journals in his lifetime and authored many books and monographs.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://jacobsschool.ucsd.edu/news/news_releases/release.sfe?id=691 |title=UCSD Engineering Dynamo Honored by National Academy Of Engineering |publisher=Jacobsschool.ucsd.edu |access-date=2017-05-08}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oac.cdlib.org/findaid/ark:/13030/kt496nb0c1/entire_text/ |title=Stanford S. Penner Papers MSS 457 |publisher=Oac.cdlib.org |access-date=2017-05-08}}</ref>
